title: Prognostic Determinants and Scoring Systems in Fournier Gangrene: A Narrative Review
content: Background: Fournier’s gangrene (FG) is a rapidly progressive necrotizing soft-tissue infection associated with substantial mortality despite modern surgical, antimicrobial, and critical-care management. Objective: To synthesize the evidence supporting clinical determinants, FG-specific severity scores, LRINEC, inflammatory biomarkers, general critical-care and comorbidity instruments, and emerging mortality indices in FG. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for publications from 1980 to 2026 using terms related to FG, necrotizing fasciitis, mortality prediction, FGSI, UFGSI, SFGSI, LRINEC, NLR, SOFA/qSOFA, NEWS2, APACHE, Charlson indices, Surgical Apgar Score, FGMI, and FGMI-2P. Original derivation studies, validation cohorts, comparative studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were prioritized. Diagnostic instruments were considered separately from mortality-prediction tools, and retained quantitative claims were checked against their cited primary sources. Results: Large syntheses place FG mortality at approximately 16–20%, with one 25-year review reporting 19.8% mortality among 6,152 cases and no significant temporal improvement [8]. FGSI, UFGSI, and SFGSI remain the best-established FG-specific composite scores; a 40-study meta-analysis reported pooled AUCs of 0.90, 0.94, and 0.84, respectively [21]. LRINEC was developed for diagnosis of necrotizing fasciitis and performs less consistently for mortality prediction in FG [19,20,25,27]. NLR is associated with mortality at thresholds of ≥8 and ≥10 but is best regarded as an adjunct rather than a stand-alone score [73]. CCI/ACCI, SOFA/qSOFA, NEWS2, and APACHE II add information on comorbidity and systemic severity, whereas FGMI and FGMI-2P are promising newer indices requiring further external validation [20,27,28,49,54,60]. Conclusions: Prognostic assessment in FG is best approached as multidimensional. FG-specific scores should be interpreted together with organ dysfunction, comorbidity burden, and inflammatory/nutritional markers. No prognostic score should delay resuscitation, broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, or urgent surgical source control.
